transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. I came in because... well, I’m just tired all the time. And I mean, I teach, so I know what it feels like to be tired at the end of the day, but this isn't that normal teacher tired. It's more like... even after a full night’s sleep, I have to really push myself just to get through grading, making dinner, and getting ready for the next morning. It just never really goes away.
Has anyone who sleeps near you—like a partner or family member—ever told you that you snore loudly or seem to stop breathing for moments while you sleep?
No, no one has ever told me that. My husband hasn't mentioned anything about me snoring loudly or stopping breathing or anything like that. I'm pretty sure I sleep quietly.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down, sad, or have you noticed you're not enjoying things you used to enjoy?

Yeah, I have. Most days I can still smile for my students and get through the lessons fine, but... underneath it all, it feels like there’s this gray, flat feeling. It just follows me home. And as for enjoying things, yeah, even my garden or doing my watercolors just seem really far away lately.
How long have you been feeling this way—the low, flat mood and losing interest in things like gardening or painting?

It's been going on for a while. I'd say... about two years and two months now. It started right around the time my husband stopped working outside the home. Our whole household routine changed back then, and that's really when I noticed this feeling starting to settle in.
Have you noticed any unintended weight gain or feeling unusually cold over the past couple of years?
No, I haven't noticed anything like that. My weight has stayed pretty much the same, and I haven't felt unusually cold or anything.
Over the past several months, have you found yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things, more than you feel you should, and having trouble controlling that worry?

No, not really. I mean, I worry about normal things, like my students or paying the bills, but it's not excessive. I wouldn't say I have trouble controlling it. It's really just that flat, low feeling that's the main issue.
Have you noticed being unusually thirsty or needing to urinate more often than usual over the past several months?
No, I haven't noticed anything like that either. My thirst and... bathroom habits seem completely normal to me.
Have you noticed that you get unusually short of breath or your heart races with activities that didn't used to bother you, like climbing stairs or walking briskly?

No, I haven't had any issues with that. I mean, I'm on my feet a lot at school, walking around the classroom and the halls, and I haven't noticed getting out of breath or my heart racing. Physically, my breathing and everything feels fine.
Have you noticed your skin, gums, or nail beds looking unusually pale, or have you felt lightheaded or dizzy, especially when standing up quickly?
No, my skin and nails look normal to me. And I don't really get dizzy or lightheaded when I stand up. None of that has been happening.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient describes a chronic, persistent low, flat mood and anhedonia (loss of interest in gardening and painting) lasting continuously for over 2 years, with onset tied to a psychosocial stressor (husband leaving work). Symptoms are present most days but are not of the severity or episodic character of a major depressive episode, and she is able to maintain functioning (teaching, smiling for students) despite the underlying dysphoria. Medical causes (hypothyroidism, diabetes, anemia, sleep apnea) and anxiety disorder (GAD) were explicitly ruled out through review of systems, supporting a primary mood disorder. The chronicity (>2 years), persistent depressive affect, and anhedonia without meeting full MDD criteria are most consistent with Persistent Depressive Disorder (Dysthymia).
